data.description:
The deterministic half of v1's definition of done. An automated test that drives the product's own HTTP API through the entire Rule-1 chain — sign up, connect an account, generate a contract, create and finalize and send an invoice, apply a paid webhook, observe paid status — on the local docker-compose stack, with NO external accounts.

IMPLEMENTS: docs/engineering/00-d1-v1-milestone-plan.md section 3 row C-05 (IN by mandate — v1 definition of done, section 6.1).

DECISION CONTEXT. This cannot run against stripe-mock alone. stripe-mock validates request and response SHAPES against Stripe's OpenAPI spec, but it is stateless and emits no webhooks (docs/strategy/spikes/spike-D1-freelancer-invoicing.md section 1). So this task extends the transport fake introduced by the custody-guard task into a STATEFUL Stripe double: it holds account, customer and invoice state, transitions invoices on finalize/send/pay, and emits correctly signed webhook payloads into the webhook receiver. Where shapes matter, keep validating against stripe-mock; where state matters, use the double. Name the two clearly in the tests, because the honest claim of this task is "our half of the loop is correct against OUR MODEL of Stripe" — and the fidelity of that model is exactly what the test-mode acceptance run exists to check. Overstating this task's guarantee is the failure mode to avoid.

VERIFICATION: the suite runs green from a clean checkout with the network unavailable, and turns red if any single step of the chain regresses.

NOT IN THIS TASK: anything requiring a real Stripe account (the acceptance-run task, which is board-gated); browser or UI automation — this drives the API deliberately, so that it stays runnable while the UI tasks are still gated on AS-30 and so a design stall cannot stall verification; performance or load testing (no capability row — v1 has one user).

data.body:
Plan written (cto-owen, on Opus under the Fable fallback; tick watcher:79108 loop tick 8). Plan: .lattice/plans/task_01M1D34P9NGTNK5A0PNPJJH98Z.md, commit be33bca. Branch feat/AS-49-e2e-loop cut from master 8161844, linked, worktree .worktrees/AS-49.

DESIGN. The stateful double is a TRANSPORT function injected at the AS-38 seam (createStripeClient({ transport })), so the real pipeline — custody guard included — runs on every call; it cannot be anything else because baseUrl is an option, never configuration, so the shipped web container cannot be pointed at a double and a separate e2e service would need the knob AS-38 refused. The e2e file boots the app in-process via withServer inside the test service (network_mode: none), same as every route suite and the AS-90 demo; it runs unskipped and identically in test and contract. Files: test/helpers/stripe-double.js (new, <=450 lines: accounts/customers/items/invoices state, nine handlers = the custody allowlist exactly, idempotency-window replay, accumulating amount_due, completeOnboarding/pay/failNth, events signed by its own node:crypto HMAC from per-transition snapshots — never sharing code with the verifier under test; two clocks: signature t is real Date.now, event data times are a fixed model clock so paidAt etc. are committed literals) and test/e2e-loop.test.js (new, <=800 lines, cases E0–E5). harness.test.js list 17->18; README § The suite gains 'The loop half (the stateful double)' with the honest-claim wording verbatim and 'three mock-gated files' -> four. ZERO app source, compose, Dockerfile, demo or dependency-policy change — asserted at review by git diff master -- test/dependency-policy.test.js being empty. Demo SEQUENCE lifted by copy (order, fixed values, request bodies), never by import; demo untouched. Delivery of signed bytes is the test's (loopback POST /webhooks/stripe), never the double's — mirrors the real topology and keeps the double socket-free.

HONEST CLAIM (plan §2, verbatim in three places, pinned as exported STRIPE_DOUBLE_CLAIM): our half of the loop is correct against OUR MODEL of Stripe; stripe-mock validates request SHAPES and answers statelessly, the double holds STATE and validates nothing, neither is Stripe; fidelity of the model is what AS-50 checks. Every case title carries '(STRIPE DOUBLE)'.

CASES / CRITERIA. E0 double table == ALLOWED_ENDPOINTS (cardinality 9). E1 the twelve steps over the API: signup+session; connect start (2 platform calls, row not ready); return not trusted; readiness by PUSH (account.updated -> ok: readiness, syncedAt = event.created) AND by PULL (second return agrees, 2 account reads); client; contract (renderedHtml occurrence counts); draft (zero Stripe calls); finalize (5 connected calls in order, mirror open, amountDue 12500 = total, finalizedAt literal); send (EXACTLY ONE call — the assertion stripe-mock structurally cannot make; then invoice.sent -> ok: fields with sentAt unchanged); paid (ok: applied, paidAt literal); redelivery (ok: duplicate, row deepEqual incl. updatedAt, one ledger row); out-of-order invoice.finalized after paid (ok: stale); whole run 10 calls, every url.origin https://api.stripe.com, 4 platform/6 connected headers, no FORBIDDEN_PARAMS segment in any wire body. E2 transient 502 on the 2nd invoiceitems push, retry completes with 3 calls, 1 replay hit, no duplicate objects. E3 tampered v1 -> 400 applies nothing; wrong-secret double -> 400; then the real one applies. E4 readiness gate inside the loop (403 not-ready, zero connected calls, then ready, then 303). E5 (contract only, skip offline): the double's account/customer/invoice key sets are SUBSETS of stripe-mock's spec-derived fixtures — the model can drift by omission, never by invention. AC-19..21 documentation checks by reviewer grep.

FALSIFIERS (plan §7): 16 recipes, each with an anchor (grep -c = 1), the edit, and the predicted e2e red set (owning-suite reds to be recorded exactly): F1 signup, F2 no connected row, F3 readiness handler, F4 contract clientName, F5 draft Location (anchored to the createDraft line; grep -c 'return detailPath' must read 3), F6 finalize predicate, F7 send predicate, F8 invoice.paid row, F9 recordOnce guard, F10 verifier accepts anything, F10b wrong-secret double, F11 transfer_data in ensureInvoice (guard fires, zero double calls), F12 stale-rank line, F-NET (route one endpoint to the real fetchTransport: 502 network in BOTH services — offline-ness proven by a red), F-ALLOW, F-REPLAY, F-SHAPE, F-V2.

RECEIPTS. Baseline master 8161844 today, -p asc-plan-as49, --build, /usr/local/bin/docker, torn down -v --rmi local: test 420/402/0/18 and contract 420/420/0/0, both 'Image asc-plan-as49-* Built' (log scratchpad/agent-cto-owen/as49/baseline-master.log). Predicted after: test 426/407/0/19, contract 426/426/0/0 (E1 split into per-step cases would raise both by the split count — restate before running).

SEAMS. AS-46 and AS-47 both edit test/harness.test.js (list + V2 literal) — certain, trivial conflict: union the lists, literal = length. README adjacent-hunk possible. AS-46 rewrites routes/invoices.js and routes/clients.js: Location pins at AC-6/8/9/10 are route-table facts, re-checked at rebase, never dereferenced (API only). Merge order AS-46 -> AS-47 -> AS-49; AS-49 may start before AS-46 merges (independent files) and MUST rebase + re-run both receipts before review.

STAFFING. Implementer developer-lena (free once AS-46 clears Ruben's cycle 2; if it comes back for rework she returns to AS-46 first). Reviewer qa-priya (Ruben on AS-46; Priya reviewed the receiver in AS-44 and reads this cold). Tasking rule: give Priya the criteria and the recipe NAMES, never the predicted red sets or the receipt numbers (AS-36). M6 seeds for the orchestrator to hold: a void event after paid (the same-rank conflict), a second freelancer's session against the first's invoice mid-loop.

OPEN (time-boxed, defaults apply): Q1 converge the older per-suite fixtures onto the double — no, this task. Q2 stateful demo variant — no. Q3 dedicated e2e compose service — no (zero compose change is a property). Q4 claim pinned as exported constant + reviewer grep (README is host-only, a test cannot read it in the image). Q5 note for AS-50's planner: E1's committed call order and the double's events are the natural 'expected' column for the acceptance run.
